x: It is odd that all the runners who have stayed there produced thier best form when at No. 4. Current lodgers are John Roberts and Ferdie Gilson of SLH, who are also running better than ever.
The 3 miles was an exciting race for after several laps of normal type pace,John "Maybe the Greatest" Roberts (SLH) decided to do a 'Clarke'.

Would John Roberts (SLH) beat Gerry North for the individual title? As the 138 runners were sent on their way, Roberts went straight into the lead and after 2 miles he was still there, followed closely by Gerry, who was in turn pursued by a small pack including Gowan (HHH), Robinson (Guildford) and Thresher (Belgrave).
Gerry was finding the going tough and had to give way to John Roberts (SLH) and Peter Yates (Windsor & Eton) and brother Geoff also lost some ground.
The time of 28:34.2 broke his own County Record by 14 seconds. John Roberts was a worthy 2nd just outside 29 minutes and Robinson 3rd.
John Roberts (SLH) beat Adrian Major in the mile but only by 0.9secs. and Bob Couillaut leapt to 21'6" in the Long Jump, improving by over a foot.

RESULT: 1.R.Taylor (Coventry) 32:34 2.R.Hill (Bolton) 32:48 3.Gerry North(BELS) 33:00 16.J.Thresher (BELS) 33:45 58.G.Williams (BELS) 34:30 BOTTOM: Thresher battles it out with Peter Hall in the Inter-Counties at Leicester, with Surrey team-mate John Roberts "sitting-in".

At the end of the first lap Gerry had a fifty yard lead having been headed only by John Roberts for a short period at about two miles. Tony Fairclough in inimitable style was seventh and Adrian Major and Laurie O'Hara were 16th and 17th.
Bob Gevers and John Roberts struck a fine blow for South London by taking the first two places, with the Croydon pair of Don Faircloth and Fred Stebbings in the next two.
